recall.define: Define deadline, remaining budget, retry budget, fencing and quiescence.
recall.distinguish: Distinguish admission from effect/delivery, cancellation from acknowledgement and rate from concurrent capacity.
recall.apply: A timed-out request commits, a hedge wins, and its loser remains active while a queue is full. Trace every retained resource and legal recovery.

entries.definition: A time bound in a specified clock domain after which a request no longer admits waiting or work under its contract.

authority.locator: Overview; Deadlines on the Server; Deadline Propagation

edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: A deadline names an expiry instant in one clock domain; a timeout specifies the duration of a particular wait or operation. Repeated waits must use the remaining duration to preserve the same deadline, and neither expiry nor a timed-out wait proves the operation stopped.

idiom: State the deadline invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: A raw monotonic timestamp cannot be compared across unrelated hosts.

entries.definition: A duration still available after accounting for elapsed work and declared propagation costs.

authority.locator: Overview; Deadlines on the Server; Deadline Propagation

edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: Remaining budget deducts work already elapsed and the declared propagation costs from one inherited allowance. Starting each hop with a fresh full timeout resets that accounting and can extend the end-to-end duration; transport delay still needs an explicit bound or uncertainty statement.

idiom: State the remaining budget invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Giving every hop a new full timeout extends the end-to-end budget.

entries.definition: Evidence that a previously admitted operation has reached a terminal state and released its borrowing obligations.

distinguish_from.distinction: A request changes cancellation state and asks an operation to stop. Acknowledgement establishes the terminal access/release event required by the adapter; RZScope cancellation alone supplies no such completion event and cannot authorize freeing borrowed storage.

idiom: State the cancellation acknowledgement invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Setting a cancellation flag does not permit freeing worker state.

entries.definition: A protocol that makes producer progress depend on consumer capacity rather than allowing unconstrained outstanding work.

authority.locator: Overview: receiver capacity, write completion and buffering

edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: Backpressure constrains admission or producer progress using receiver capacity. Packet loss merely describes missing delivery and can occur without any capacity feedback. RZ_BLOCK retains a pending offer, whereas RZ_DROP consumes that offer without enqueueing it; the number of pending producers must also be bounded.

idiom: State the backpressure invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: A bounded queue can coexist with unbounded producer-held memory.

entries.definition: The declared behavior when offered work exceeds available admission capacity.

authority.locator: Overview: receiver capacity, write completion and buffering

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: An overload policy specifies observable behavior when capacity is exhausted: wait, reject, drop, overwrite or coalesce. Throughput optimization concerns processing cost under a fixed correctness contract; substituting coalescing for reliable delivery changes that contract even if the measured rate improves.

idiom: State the overload policy invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Dropping and coalescing change observations even if throughput improves.

entries.definition: An explicit permission to consume a bounded amount of receiver capacity, conserved across admission and release.

authority.locator: Overview: receiver capacity, write completion and buffering

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: A flow credit authorizes bounded admission and is returned according to the capacity-release protocol. It is not evidence that the corresponding application effect committed: RZService distinguishes notification capacity, effect commit, channel acceptance and consumer delivery.

idiom: State the flow credit invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: A capacity credit does not mean an application effect completed.

entries.definition: A group of candidate timers selected by a modular time index; a full expiry discriminator distinguishes different revolutions.

authority.locator: Section5 pp29-30: bounded wheel and doubly linked cancellation

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: Bucket selection compares time modulo the wheel size, so different absolute expiries share a bucket. With four buckets, due times1 and5 both map to bucket1; the tick1 visit must still test the full due time before reporting the timer due at5.

idiom: State the timer-wheel bucket invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Sharing a bucket does not make timers due together.

entries.definition: Movement of a coarse timer into a finer timing level as its expiry approaches.

authority.locator: Section5 pp29-30: bounded wheel and doubly linked cancellation

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: A cascade in the required hierarchical-wheel extension moves a timer into a finer scheduling level while preserving its identity and absolute due time. It does not run the callback or itself establish expiry. The supplied one-level anchor only returns due-slot bits and invokes no callbacks.

idiom: State the timer cascade invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Cascading a timer does not itself imply its deadline has arrived.

entries.definition: Stored token capacity that permits a bounded admission burst beyond the replenishment rate over a short interval.

authority.locator: ALGORITHM: initial burst, steady refill, finite queue and peak bucket

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: Burst credit is stored token capacity spent at admission and replenished with elapsed time. A concurrency limit instead caps operations that still retain active permits; slow operations can accumulate despite a bounded admission rate unless that separate ownership limit is enforced.

idiom: State the burst credit invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: A rate bound does not limit all long-running active requests.

entries.definition: Computing accumulated resource credit at an observed time rather than updating it on every clock tick.

authority.locator: ALGORITHM: initial burst, steady refill, finite queue and peak bucket

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: Lazy refill computes accrued tokens when the bucket is observed, but clamps them to the declared capacity. Arbitrarily long idle time cannot create unlimited credit; the overflow-safe calculation must saturate before an overflowing elapsed-times-rate multiplication.

idiom: State the lazy refill invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Long idle time fills only to the declared capacity.

entries.definition: A limit on extra attempts or resources spent after an original request fails or becomes uncertain.

authority.locator: Timeouts: whole-call scope and connection setup

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: The retry budget bounds admitted extra attempts or their shared resource cost. Backoff only changes their scheduling delay: even a zero-delay retry consumes one RZRetry attempt, and an increasing delay sequence alone does not establish a finite attempt count.

idiom: State the retry budget invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Increasing delays alone does not bound total attempts.

entries.definition: Variation in retry scheduling intended to reduce correlated simultaneous demand under a stated randomization model.

authority.locator: Timeouts: whole-call scope and connection setup

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: Jitter spreads attempted start times according to a stated draw model. Idempotency concerns the effect of repeated requests; random delays do not prevent duplicate effects. RZRetry requires a separate safe-to-repeat assertion, and RZReceiver supplies only its explicitly bounded deduplication guarantee.

idiom: State the retry jitter invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Random timing does not make duplicate side effects safe.

entries.definition: A bounded admission used to test recovery after a circuit breaker open period.

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: A half-open probe is one controlled current-epoch request after cooldown, not permission for every waiting caller to run. RZGate allows at most one such probe while retaining its separate active-permit limit; old-epoch completions release capacity without deciding the new epoch's health.

idiom: State the half-open probe invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Expiry of cooldown must not release an unlimited probe burst.

entries.definition: An admission boundary that limits simultaneous retained resource ownership, optionally reserving capacity between tenants.

authority.locator: Configure a Bulkhead: maxConcurrentCalls and maxWaitDuration

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: A bulkhead counts active retained permits until terminal completion. A failure-rate window summarizes outcomes to decide health/admission policy and does not itself bound active work. RZGate combines a one-or-two-permit bulkhead with a separate consecutive-failure rule; its sliding-window variant must preserve that separation.

idiom: State the bulkhead invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: A health sample window is not a concurrent-execution limit.

entries.definition: An additional overlapping attempt intended to obtain an acceptable response sooner while retaining ownership of every started attempt.

authority.locator: Retry semantics: overall timeout and retry budgets

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: A hedge deliberately admits another attempt while the original may remain active. A strictly sequential retry starts only after the prior attempt terminates; a timeout by itself does not prove that termination. RZHedge may publish a winner while still retaining the losing attempt until its own completion.

idiom: State the hedged request invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Choosing a winner does not terminate the loser.

entries.definition: The state in which every started operation has terminated its access to the resources proposed for reclamation.

authority.locator: WithDeadline: earlier parent deadline and cancellation

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: Result availability means a response can be consumed; quiescence means every started attempt has ended its access to the retained resources. An RZHedge winner makes the result available immediately, but a cancellation request to its loser does not set that loser's completion bit.

idiom: State the operation quiescence invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: A useful result can be available while another attempt still borrows memory.

entries.definition: The explicitly bounded retention interval in which a request identity maps to its original effect and result.

authority.locator: Reducing client complexity: caller request identifier and atomic token/effect

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: A deduplication window retains an original request/result mapping only for its specified lifetime. RZReceiver expires records at age>=window, so the same identifier may apply again afterward; volatile retention also does not survive restart or establish indefinite exactly-once effects.

idiom: State the deduplication window invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: An expired identity may be admitted again.

entries.definition: A monotonically ordered authority marker checked by the protected resource to reject writes from older owners.

authority.locator: Making the lock safe with fencing: resource checks increasing tokens

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: A fencing token carries an order that the protected resource actually checks against its highest admitted authority. A random lease ID can distinguish holders without ordering them, so uniqueness alone cannot reject an older holder after a newer owner acts. Token issuance, authentication and restart ordering remain separate obligations.

idiom: State the fencing token invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Uniqueness does not establish an ordering or prevent a stale write.

entries.definition: Owned notification state reserved or durably recorded alongside an effect so later delivery has an explicit recovery path.

authority.locator: Reducing client complexity: caller request identifier and atomic token/effect

edition_notes.edition: C17 mechanism and bounded library comparison
edition_notes.note: Runtime protocol and explicit ownership assumptions; ISO C does not automatically implement the service guarantee.

distinguish_from.distinction: An outbox retains responsibility for an effect's notification across a failed or delayed send. A successful local send establishes only the transport's stated acceptance, not consumer delivery or durable effect/notification commit. RZService reserves a volatile pending slot before committing its synthetic effect; crash-safe outbox recovery is a separate required extension.

idiom: State the committed notification outbox invariant before selecting a representation or accepting work.
entries.misconception: Volatile queued state does not survive a crash merely because the effect committed.
